To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

semantic priming in the naming of Italian and English words was investigated, and that in the Italian experiment, the inclusion of a few pseudowords in a list prevented the priming effects from appearing, but in the English experiment, this did not occur.

the lexical status of the prime and of the target is crucial for the occurrence of semantic priming in naming, and that the writing systems in which the experiments are conducted are important in determining the conditions under which lexical reading occurs
the lexical decision task and pronunciation are different in that the lexical decision can be performed on pseudowords, but the pronunciation of pseudowords is impossible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the nature of the writing system may interact with the characteristics of the reading process.
the role of writing in reading aloud.
the interaction between the characteristics of the writing system and the characteristics of the language, and the effects of this interaction on reading strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the writing system is a relevant factor in determining the reading strategy that people use in the pronunciation of written words.
the writing system plays a crucial role in the way in which words are read.
, in general, the writing systems are relevant in determining whether or not the pronunciation of words can be based on a nonlexical route.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lexical route is used in reading, but that it can be bypassed if it is not needed.
, when reading, the reader does not have a choice between a lexical and a nonlexical reading route; instead, the reader uses lexical reading.

, in Italian, lexical reading is the normal strategy, and that the presence of pseudowords does not prevent the occurrence of semantic priming effects, but it prevents priming from affecting pronunciation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when reading is not lexical, semantic effects are not obtained in the pronunciation task.
reading aloud is not a simple task, but one that requires a number of cognitive processes to be performed. In
the writing systems of different languages can affect the way in which the same cognitive processes are implemented.
